COMMITTEE DISCHARGED AND COMMITTED TO RULES
ORDERED TO THIRD READING RULES CAL.204

items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the insurance law, in relation to the designation of third parties to receive notification of cancellation
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S2268

TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the insurance law, in relation to the designation of
third parties to receive notification of cancellation

PURPOSE:

To enhance the protections currently afforded to senior citizen
insureds by requiring that the people designated by a senior citizen
insured as the third party who will receive a copy of a notice of
cancellation for nonpayment of premium to receive such notice no less
than thirty days before the effective date of the cancelation.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section one provides paragraph 6 of subsection (b) of section 1117 of
the insurance law is amended through the addition of a new
subparagraph (F) which would allow the prospective insured who is 65
years of age or older to designate a third party who will receive a
copy of the notice of cancellation sent to the prospective insured.

Section two of this bill amends subsection (e) of section 3111 of the
insurance law to allow senior citizens who purchases long-term care
insurance as defined in section 1117 of this chapter and for which the
senior citizen pays for directly to the insurer shall permit the
senior citizen to designate a third whom the insurer shall send a copy
of the notice of cancellation prior to the effective date of the
cancellation and proscribes the manner in which the senior citizen
shall notify the insurer of the chosen designated third party.
Additionally this section will now provide that if a senior citizen
has not made a third party designation the insurer shall include a
copy of the third party designation form with each premium statement
sent to the senior citizen. This subsection now requires the insurer
to confirm that the third party designee's contact information is
correct. If the insurer receives designation or termination of a
designation the insurer shall verify such action in the manner
prescribed.

Section three provides that this act shall take effect on the sixtieth
day after it shall have become a law.

JUSTIFICATION:

This bill enhances the current statutory scheme allowing senior
citizens who hold long term care insurance policies to designate a
third party to receive notices of nonpayment of premiums due or
notices of cancelation for nonpayment of premiums. This bill would
require insurers to send a copy of the notice of cancelation for
nonpayment of premium to be sent to the third party designee no later
than thirty days before the effective date of the cancelation.
Current law allows insurers to determine when notices will be sent to
third party designees. If the notices are not received in a timely
manner, third party designation safeguard has failed.


Section two of the bill further enhances these protections by
prescribing the manner in which a third party designee may be chosen
and the process the insurer may use to confirm designation or
termination of designation and requires the insurer to confirm that
the contact information of the third party designate is correct.
These additional safeguards will strengthen the protection that the
law currently provides our senior citizens.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2014: S.7506 - Reported to Finance

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

Undetermined.

EFFECTIVE DATE:

This act shall take effect on the sixtieth day after it shall have
become a law on the sixtieth day after it shall have become a law.

summary: Authorizes an insured to designate a third party to receive cancellation notification.
